subject: Biotechnology
title: Enzymatic Textile Waste Recycling
description: A micro-lesson that makes Enzymatic Textile Waste Recycling usable.

hook.text: 92 million tons of textiles are discarded annually — enzymes can separate blended fibers that mechanical recycling cannot handle.

buildup.text: Cellulase enzymes selectively digest cotton in cotton-polyester blends — leaving clean polyester fibers for recycling.

discovery.text: Protease enzymes break down wool and silk — recovering amino acids for new materials without harsh chemical processing.

twist.text: Dyes and finishes interfere with enzymatic digestion — pretreatment to remove chemicals adds cost and complexity.

climax.text: Carbios and Worn Again Technologies scale enzymatic textile recycling — closing the loop on fashion's waste crisis.

punchline.text: Enzymes untangle your old clothes — biological recycling separates what machines cannot.

quiz.question: Why are enzymes useful for recycling blended fabrics?
options: They can melt both natural and synthetic fibers simultaneously
They selectively digest one fiber type like cotton while leaving the other like polyester intact for recycling
They permanently remove all dyes and make fabrics reusable
